questions.q: What advantage does the lesson say blockchain work has over most other engineering disciplines on a resume?
options: A deployed, verified contract can be checked by a stranger for free, in about thirty seconds
Blockchain projects never need to be tested before shipping
Smart contracts cannot be reviewed by anyone outside the original team
Blockchain resumes never need links to any external proof
questions.explain: The lesson opens by naming public, verifiable, tamper-evident deployment as blockchain's unique resume advantage.

questions.q: What three things does the action + artifact + proof pattern require a resume bullet to include?
options: What you did, what you built, and where a reviewer can verify it
Your job title, your start date, and your manager's name
The company's total revenue and headcount
A list of every blockchain you have ever heard of
questions.explain: The lesson defines the pattern as action, artifact, and proof -- with proof meaning a verifiable link like Etherscan or a repo.

questions.q: In the lesson's suggested one-page structure, what comes right after the header and optional summary?
options: The three capstone projects, each with proof-backed bullets and a verification link
A full list of every programming language ever studied
References from previous employers
A certificate gallery with no further detail
questions.explain: The structure places the three capstone projects early, since they carry the strongest, most specific proof of ability.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against calling a project 'deployed' when it has only ever run locally?
options: Because a resume should be precise about verification status, and overstating it is a credibility risk
Because local projects are always lower quality than deployed ones
Because 'deployed' is a reserved Solidity keyword
Because local-only projects cannot be tested at all
questions.explain: The lesson lists overstating deployment status as one of the common mistakes that weakens a blockchain developer resume.

questions.q: How should a candidate decide which of their three capstones to lead with for a specific job posting?
options: By checking which chain, framework, and specialty the posting emphasizes, and leading with the closest match
By always leading with whichever project took the least time to build
By listing all three in strictly alphabetical order every time
By omitting all three and relying on a buzzword list instead
questions.explain: The lesson's tailoring section recommends matching the posting's emphasis (chain, framework, specialty) when choosing which project to lead with.
